purpose: Semantic MIDI export corpus. Entries with insufficient independent evidence are explicitly unresolved; labels are never guessed.

entries.reviewNotes: Tracker emits 200/100 (half/double family) BPM; Exact symbolic capture and the librosa reference disagree on tempo; dense FM evidence does not establish a unique meter or downbeat.

Deterministic control generated at 120 BPM in 4/4. Evidence redesigned to be decisive: asymmetric backbeat (kick 2.0 on the bar downbeat, snare 1.0 on beat 2, snare 0.25 on beat 4, NO accent on beat 3, hi-hat on 8ths) plus bass on the bar downbeat. The asymmetry kills the half/double-tempo alternatives (Ellis 120 with no alternative), and the bar-periodic accent pins the downbeat. DBN fixes (resolved-candidate selection, downbeat snap to structural boundary, uniform-path override for the resolved tempo) make the exact reading 120 BPM / 4/4 / downbeat quarter 0, asserted EXACTLY here.

Deterministic control generated at exactly 90 BPM in 6/8, asserted EXACTLY (bpm 90, 6/8, downbeat quarter 0). WHY 90 IS HONEST AND REACHABLE: (1) librosa/Ellis half-BPM beat bins include 90, so tempo=90 IS a member of the hypothesis set — it is not hop-quantized away (the earlier '91 is the nearest reachable reading' premise was false); (2) with the PhaseScores normalization fix (integer division count/cycle inflated coarse-grid downbeat scores past 1.0) and the joint slow-tempo bias removed, the 90 BPM 6/8 hypothesis OUT-SCORES 91 and every slow-tempo alternative; (3) the control was generated at exactly 90 BPM, so the exact assertion tests the tracker's reading against ground truth — we assert exact truth, we do not adapt the assertion to the output. Evidence follows the reviewed recipe: strong accents at compound beats 1 and 4 (kick 1.5 / 0.8), subdivisions on eighths, bass at bar boundaries, no 4/4 backbeat symmetry.

Deterministic control generated at 100 BPM in 3/4, asserted EXACTLY (bpm 100, 3/4, downbeat quarter 0). Evidence: kick 2.0 on beat 1, snare 1.0 on beats 2 and 3, hi-hat on beats with 8th subdivisions, bass on beat 1. The PhaseScores normalization fix (integer division count/cycle inflated coarse-grid downbeat scores past 1.0) and the pattern-primary meterEvidence (accent pattern flips 3/4 above the 6/8-at-half-tempo reading) remove the slow-tempo bias that previously read this as 6/8 at 50 BPM; the tracker now lands on the exact 100 BPM 3/4 reading with the downbeat on quarter 0.
